title: NYC Process Server Individual License Exam
page_numbering: PDF page index (1 = first page of the PDF file); null for HTML pages

questions.question: How many questions are on the Process Server Individual exam?
questions.explanation: The exam has 35 multiple-choice questions.

source.title: DCWP: Process Server Individual License Application Checklist
source.quote: The exam consists of 35 multiple choice questions.

questions.question: What is the minimum number of correct answers needed to pass the Process Server Individual exam?
questions.explanation: You must answer no fewer than 25 of the 35 questions correctly.

source.title: DCWP Frequently Asked Questions: Exams (PDF)
source.quote: To pass the exam, you must correctly answer no fewer than 25 questions.

questions.question: What is the Process Server Individual exam fee?
options: $75, separate from the license fee and nonrefundable
$50, refundable once you pass the exam
$340, the same as the license fee
Nothing extra; it is included in the license fee
questions.explanation: The exam fee is $75, separate from the license fee and nonrefundable.

source.title: DCWP: Process Server Individual License Application Checklist
source.quote: The fee is $75. The exam fee is separate from the license fee and is nonrefundable.

questions.question: Who must take the Process Server Individual exam?
questions.explanation: Unlike the HIC and guide exams, the process server exam is required for new AND renewing applicants.

source.title: DCWP Frequently Asked Questions: Exams (PDF)
source.quote: Process Server Individual (NEW and RENEWING applicants)

questions.question: What happens if a process server applicant fails the exam twice?
options: They pay $50 for two more tries
They must reapply for the license
They take a DCWP course instead
They wait 30 days and retry free
questions.explanation: After two failures the application is denied and the applicant must reapply for the license, paying the fees again.

source.title: DCWP: Process Server Individual License Application Checklist
source.quote: If you fail the exam twice, you must reapply for the license

questions.question: Does a second attempt at the process server exam cost an additional fee?
questions.explanation: An applicant who fails the first time may take the exam a second time without an additional fee.

source.title: DCWP Educational Materials for Process Servers (PDF, updated 3/3/2025)
source.quote: may take the examination a second time without an additional fee.

questions.question: Once your information appears in ExamBuilder's system, how long do you have to take and pass the exam?
questions.explanation: You have 60 days from the time your information appears in ExamBuilder's system.

source.title: DCWP: Process Server Individual License Application Checklist
source.quote: You have 60 days to take and pass the exam from the time your information appears in ExamBuilder’s system.

questions.question: After failing your first attempt, how long must you wait before scheduling the second?
questions.explanation: You must wait 24 hours from the failed attempt before scheduling again.

source.title: DCWP Frequently Asked Questions: Exams (PDF)
source.quote: You must wait 24 hours from your failed attempt before scheduling the exam for a second attempt.

questions.question: Which of these is listed as acceptable ID at the ExamBuilder Test Center?
options: A recent utility bill with your address
A public library card with your name
A credit card that shows your photo
questions.explanation: Acceptable government photo IDs with signature include a driver's license, passport, IDNYC and your DCWP Process Server Individual license.

source.title: DCWP Frequently Asked Questions: Exams (PDF)
source.quote: Your DCWP Process Server Individual license

questions.question: What happens if you miss a scheduled exam without rescheduling in advance?
questions.explanation: A no-show counts as a fail, reported to DCWP by ExamBuilder.

source.title: DCWP Frequently Asked Questions: Exams (PDF)
source.quote: If you miss a scheduled exam without rescheduling in advance, you will automatically fail

questions.question: How does DCWP describe its Educational Materials for Process Servers?
options: Optional reading unrelated to the exam
Not a study guide exclusively for the exam
A copy of the exam questions
questions.explanation: DCWP says the materials help but are not exclusively an exam study guide; consult other resources too.

source.title: DCWP Frequently Asked Questions: Exams (PDF)
source.quote: These materials are not a “study guide” exclusively for the exam.

questions.question: Which part of the NYC Marshals Handbook of Regulations does DCWP point process servers to?
questions.explanation: DCWP lists the Marshals Handbook, in particular Chapter IV, Section 2-2 and Section 5.

source.title: DCWP: Process Server Individual License Application Checklist
source.quote: New York City Marshals Handbook of Regulations, in particular Chapter IV, Section 2-2 and Section 5.

questions.question: Under General Business Law § 89-ff, what must a process server put on any affidavit of service they sign?
options: The plaintiff's name, phone number and attorney's address
Their license number and the distributing agency's name and address
Their home address, date of birth and years of experience
Their fee for the service and the time spent serving
questions.explanation: GBL § 89-ff requires the license number plus the name and address of any distributing agency (DCWP's own sample question).

source.title: DCWP Educational Materials for Process Servers (PDF, updated 3/3/2025)
source.quote: the name and address of any process serving agency from whom he obtained the process for service

questions.question: How many services of process in a calendar year require a Process Server Individual license?
questions.explanation: You need a license if you serve process five or more times in a calendar year.

source.title: DCWP: Process Server Individual License Application Checklist
source.quote: You must have a Process Server Individual license if you serve process five (5) or more times in a calendar year.

questions.question: Which of these people does NOT need a Process Server license?
options: A courier who serves eviction papers weekly
A retired police officer serving process for an agency
An attorney admitted to practice in New York State
A paralegal who serves 10 summonses a year
questions.explanation: Attorneys admitted in New York are exempt from the subchapter.

source.title: DCWP Educational Materials for Process Servers (PDF, updated 3/3/2025)
source.quote: The provisions of this subchapter shall not apply to attorneys duly admitted to practice law in the state of New York.

questions.question: A City employee serves papers as part of their job. Do they need a Process Server license?
options: No, if acting within the scope of employment
Only for papers in Housing Court cases
Only if they serve more than 5 papers a year
Yes, always, like any other process server
questions.explanation: Government employees acting within the scope of their employment are exempt.

source.title: DCWP: Process Server Individual License Application Checklist
source.quote: You are an employee of a City, State, or Federal department or agency acting within the scope of your employment.

questions.question: Does an office employee of a process server who never actually serves process need a license?
questions.explanation: Employees of a process server or attorney who do not actually serve process need no license.

source.title: DCWP Educational Materials for Process Servers (PDF, updated 3/3/2025)
source.quote: No license under Subchapter 23 shall be required of any employee of a process server or attorney who does not actually serve process.

questions.question: Where do the City's process server licensing rules apply?
options: Only to service of process within the City of New York
Anywhere a New York City case is filed
Anywhere in New York State, if the case is in NYC
Only to papers in cases filed in Manhattan courts
questions.explanation: Subchapter 23 applies only to service of process within NYC.

source.title: DCWP Educational Materials for Process Servers (PDF, updated 3/3/2025)
source.quote: The provisions of Subchapter 23 shall only apply to service of process within the City of New York.

questions.question: Under 6 RCNY § 2-231, when is a legal paper NOT "process"?
options: When mailing alone can legally serve it
When it is a subpoena for documents
When it is served on a corporation
When it is under 10 pages long
questions.explanation: If state law lets the paper be served by mail, it is not process for this subchapter.

source.title: DCWP Educational Materials for Process Servers (PDF, updated 3/3/2025)
source.quote: the mailing of such legal paper is sufficient to effect service, such legal paper will not be process

questions.question: Which of these is excluded from the definition of a process serving agency?
options: A firm that assigns papers to servers
questions.explanation: Attorneys or law firms located in the state, and city marshals, are not process serving agencies.

source.title: DCWP Educational Materials for Process Servers (PDF, updated 3/3/2025)
source.quote: other than an attorney or law firm located in this state, or city marshal

questions.question: What is the license fee for a full 24-month Process Server Individual license?
questions.explanation: The biennial license fee is $340.

source.title: DCWP: Process Server Individual License Application Checklist
source.quote: Pay $340 for a license expiring February 28 of the next even year.

questions.question: When do Process Server Individual licenses expire?
questions.explanation: Process server licenses expire February 28 in even-numbered years.

source.title: DCWP: Process Server Individual License Application Checklist
source.quote: Expiration Date: February 28 in Even Years

questions.question: An applicant filing between September 1 of an odd year and February 28 of an even year can choose a 30-month license. What does it cost?
questions.explanation: Option 2 in that window is $425 for a license valid up to 30 months.

source.title: DCWP: Process Server Individual License Application Checklist
source.quote: Option 2: Pay $425 for a license expiring February 28 of the next even year.

questions.question: What does DCWP charge to photograph an applicant at an in-person appointment?
questions.explanation: DCWP photographs license applicants at no cost.

source.title: DCWP: Process Server Individual License Application Checklist
source.quote: DCWP will photograph license applicants at no cost.

questions.question: Where must a process server upload their Roster of Process Serving Agencies?
questions.explanation: The roster is submitted with the application and uploaded to DCWP's Process Server Portal.

source.title: DCWP: Process Server Individual License Application Checklist
source.quote: you must also upload your Roster of Process Serving Agencies to DCWP's Process Server Portal

questions.question: Which certification about GPS devices must a Process Server Individual applicant submit?
questions.explanation: Applicants submit the Process Server Individual Electronic Device Certification form.

source.title: DCWP: Process Server Individual License Application Checklist
source.quote: Download the Process Server Individual Electronic Device Certification form .

questions.question: In the Recordkeeping Certification, the applicant affirms records will be retained for how long?
questions.explanation: The applicant affirms that required records will be retained for seven years.

source.title: DCWP Process Server Individual Recordkeeping Certification (PDF)
source.quote: will retain for seven (7) years all records required to be maintained in compliance with 6 RCNY section 2-233.

questions.question: What kind of email address must every process server give DCWP?
questions.explanation: Process servers must provide a regularly used email; DCWP may send licensing documents and subpoenas there.

source.title: DCWP Educational Materials for Process Servers (PDF, updated 3/3/2025)
source.quote: All process servers and process serving agencies must provide to the Department a regularly used email address.

questions.question: When DCWP suspends or revokes a process server's license, how quickly must it post this and notify all agencies?
questions.explanation: Notification and posting must happen within five days of the action.

source.title: DCWP Educational Materials for Process Servers (PDF, updated 3/3/2025)
source.quote: Such notification and posting shall occur no more than five days from the date the department has suspended, revoked or denied renewal

questions.question: A person harmed by improper service sues. When can punitive damages be awarded?
options: Only for willful failure to serve process
Never; only compensatory damages are allowed
Only in suits against process serving agencies
In every case where service was defective
questions.explanation: Punitive damages are available only for a willful failure to serve process.

source.title: DCWP Educational Materials for Process Servers (PDF, updated 3/3/2025)
source.quote: punitive damages shall only be awarded in the case of willful failure to serve process

questions.question: Whom may a person injured by improper service sue under Admin Code § 20-409.2?
options: Only the process server, not the agency
The process server and the agency that assigned the process
Only DCWP, which licensed the process server
Only the plaintiff's attorney who hired the agency
questions.explanation: The cause of action runs against the process server and the process serving agency that distributed the process.

source.title: DCWP Educational Materials for Process Servers (PDF, updated 3/3/2025)
source.quote: shall have a cause of action against such process server and process serving agency

questions.question: Which state law governs whether a criminal conviction can justify denying a process server license?
questions.explanation: Denials based on convictions follow Article 23-A of the Correction Law.

source.title: DCWP Educational Materials for Process Servers (PDF, updated 3/3/2025)
source.quote: in accordance with article twenty-three-a of the correction law

questions.question: At renewal, what must a process server certify in writing?
options: That they passed a drug test
That they served at least 100 papers
questions.explanation: Renewal applicants subject to § 20-406.3(a) certify in writing that they complied with recordkeeping rules.

source.title: DCWP Educational Materials for Process Servers (PDF, updated 3/3/2025)
source.quote: shall certify in writing compliance with the record keeping provisions of such section.

questions.question: A process server ceases to serve exclusively as an employee of an agency. How soon must they notify DCWP?
questions.explanation: Notify DCWP within five days of ceasing that exclusive employment.

source.title: DCWP Educational Materials for Process Servers (PDF, updated 3/3/2025)
source.quote: within five (5) days that he or she ceases such employment

questions.question: When renewing, which agencies must a process server report to DCWP?
options: Every agency used in the previous two years
None; agencies report their own servers
Only agencies used in the past six months
Only the agency they currently work for
questions.explanation: Renewing servers report every agency they accepted process from within the previous two years.

source.title: DCWP Educational Materials for Process Servers (PDF, updated 3/3/2025)
source.quote: from which it has accepted assignment of service of process within the previous two years.

questions.question: How long must a process server keep a list of the agencies that assign them service?
questions.explanation: Keep the list of assigning agencies for seven years and produce it on request.

source.title: DCWP Educational Materials for Process Servers (PDF, updated 3/3/2025)
source.quote: The process server must maintain the list for seven years and produce it upon request by the Department.

questions.question: How soon must a licensee respond in writing to a complaint DCWP sends it?
options: Only if a hearing is set
questions.explanation: Responses to DCWP complaints are due within 20 days of the date sent.

source.title: DCWP Educational Materials for Process Servers (PDF, updated 3/3/2025)
source.quote: The response must be made within 20 days of the date the complaint is sent to the licensee or applicant

questions.question: A process server renews 75 days after the license expired. How does DCWP treat the application?
options: As a late renewal with a $15 fee
questions.explanation: Renewals filed sixty days or more after expiration are treated as new applications.

source.title: DCWP Educational Materials for Process Servers (PDF, updated 3/3/2025)
source.quote: filed sixty days or more after the expiration date of such license shall be treated as a new license application

questions.question: Where must a licensee appear to answer a DCWP notice of hearing?
options: The Office of Administrative Trials and Hearings (OATH)
The DCWP Licensing Center at 42 Broadway
Housing Court in the borough of the violation
NYC Civil Court in the server's home county
questions.explanation: Notices of hearing are answered at OATH.

source.title: DCWP Educational Materials for Process Servers (PDF, updated 3/3/2025)
source.quote: A licensee must appear at the Office of Administrative Trials and Hearings to answer a notice of hearing

questions.question: How long must process servers retain records of each process served under Admin Code § 20-406.3?
questions.explanation: Records must be kept no less than seven years for each process served.

source.title: DCWP Educational Materials for Process Servers (PDF, updated 3/3/2025)
source.quote: for no less than seven (7) years of each process served.

questions.question: Which two ways may an individual process server keep records of service under 6 RCNY § 2-233?
options: Notes on the papers served, or texts to the agency
Bound paginated volumes, or electronic records with a third-party contractor
Loose-leaf binders, or spreadsheets on a home computer
questions.explanation: Records are kept in bound paginated volumes or as electronic records stored with a third-party contractor.

source.title: DCWP Educational Materials for Process Servers (PDF, updated 3/3/2025)
source.quote: by keeping bound paginated volumes or by storing electronic records with a third party contractor.

questions.question: A server keeps a bound paginated volume. Within how long must entries be scanned into an image file?
options: Within 24 hours of each service or attempt
Within three business days of the last event recorded
Once a month, on the first business day
At license renewal, for the whole license term
questions.explanation: Scanning must be done within three business days from the last event recorded.

source.title: DCWP Educational Materials for Process Servers (PDF, updated 3/3/2025)
source.quote: such scanning must be done within three business days from the last event recorded in the records

questions.question: How must the scanned image file of a bound volume be named?
options: With any name, as long as it is dated
With the defendant's last and first name
With the court index number only
With the service date and server's license number
questions.explanation: Image files are named with the service date and the process server's license number, and date/time stamped.

source.title: DCWP Educational Materials for Process Servers (PDF, updated 3/3/2025)
source.quote: must be named with the date of the service or attempted service recorded in the bound paginated volume and the process server's license number

questions.question: How many bound paginated volumes may a process server make entries in at the same time?
questions.explanation: Entries go in only one volume at a time until it is full.

source.title: DCWP Educational Materials for Process Servers (PDF, updated 3/3/2025)
source.quote: The process server must make entries in only one volume at a time

questions.question: How must a portable media device holding scanned records be labeled?
options: Server's last name, license number and the date range of records
The agency's name and the server's DCWP license number
No label is needed if the device is password-protected
The word "CONFIDENTIAL" and the year of the records
questions.explanation: Label it with the server's last name, license number and the date range stored.

source.title: DCWP Educational Materials for Process Servers (PDF, updated 3/3/2025)
source.quote: labeled with the process server's last name, license number and the date range of the records stored on the device

questions.question: What does "chronological" mean for process server records?
options: Entries in time order with no blank spaces
Entries grouped by the assigning agency
Entries grouped by court and county
Entries in alphabetical order by defendant
questions.explanation: Each entry is sequential by time and date, without blank spaces that would allow insertions.

source.title: DCWP Educational Materials for Process Servers (PDF, updated 3/3/2025)
source.quote: without leaving any blank spaces between each entry

questions.question: What does "contemporaneous" mean for record entries?
options: At the end of each work week, in one batch
Before the attempt is made, as a plan for the day
When the affidavit of service is filed with the court
At or near the time of the event, or within a reasonable time after
questions.explanation: Contemporaneous means at or near the time of the event recorded, or within a reasonable time thereafter.

source.title: DCWP Educational Materials for Process Servers (PDF, updated 3/3/2025)
source.quote: “Contemporaneous” in relation to entries in records means at or near the time of the event

questions.question: In what file format must an "image file" of scanned records be saved?
questions.explanation: An image file is an exact replica saved as a portable data file (pdf).

source.title: DCWP Educational Materials for Process Servers (PDF, updated 3/3/2025)
source.quote: is saved as a portable data file (“pdf”).

questions.question: How may a process server correct an error in a bound paginated volume?
options: Remove the page and recopy the day's entries
Erase it neatly and rewrite the correct information
Draw a straight line through it and print the correct information directly above
Cover it with correction fluid and write the fix on top
questions.explanation: Only a straight line through the error, with the correction printed directly above, is allowed.

source.title: DCWP Educational Materials for Process Servers (PDF, updated 3/3/2025)
source.quote: only by drawing a straight line through the inaccurate entry and clearly printing the accurate information directly above the inaccurate entry.

questions.question: Which correction methods are prohibited in bound volumes?
questions.explanation: All other methods, including erasing, opaquing, obliterating or redacting, are prohibited.

source.title: DCWP Educational Materials for Process Servers (PDF, updated 3/3/2025)
source.quote: including but not limited to erasing, opaquing, obliterating or redacting, are prohibited.

questions.question: How is an electronic record with a third-party contractor amended to fix a typo?
options: By asking the contractor to overwrite it
By a new entry citing the original in italics
By deleting the entry and re-entering it
By editing the original entry in place
questions.explanation: Amendments are new entries in which the original record is identified by reference in italics.

source.title: DCWP Educational Materials for Process Servers (PDF, updated 3/3/2025)
source.quote: creating a new entry in which the original record must be identified by reference in italics within the new entry

questions.question: Which of these is expressly prohibited for electronic process server records?
questions.explanation: Tampering with data or properties, including with a meta data scrubber, is prohibited.

source.title: DCWP Educational Materials for Process Servers (PDF, updated 3/3/2025)
source.quote: using a meta data scrubber or similar device or program

questions.question: How must a process server's license number be entered in records of service?
options: As a seven-digit number, with leading zero(s) if shorter
Exactly as printed on the license, at any length
With the prefix "DCWP-" before the number
As the last four digits of the license number
questions.explanation: The license number is a seven-digit number, padded with zero if shorter.

source.title: DCWP Educational Materials for Process Servers (PDF, updated 3/3/2025)
source.quote: specified as a seven-digit number, where the first number must be zero if the process server's license number is less than seven digits

questions.question: In what format must the date of service be entered in records?
questions.explanation: Dates are entered as MM/DD/YYYY.

source.title: DCWP Educational Materials for Process Servers (PDF, updated 3/3/2025)
source.quote: the date that service was attempted or effected, which must be entered as MM/DD/YYYY

questions.question: In what format must the time of service be entered?
questions.explanation: Times are entered in military time.

source.title: DCWP Educational Materials for Process Servers (PDF, updated 3/3/2025)
source.quote: the time service was attempted or effected, which must be entered as military time

questions.question: Into how many fields must the service address be split in the records?
questions.explanation: Building number, street name, address details, city or borough, and ZIP code: five fields.

source.title: DCWP Educational Materials for Process Servers (PDF, updated 3/3/2025)
source.quote: which must be entered in five different fields

questions.question: How is whether service was effected recorded?
options: Y for yes or N for no
questions.explanation: Records show whether service was effected with Y or N.

source.title: DCWP Educational Materials for Process Servers (PDF, updated 3/3/2025)
source.quote: whether service was effected, as indicated by a Y for yes or N for no

questions.question: For service under CPLR 308(1)-(3), how many fields must the description of the person served have?
questions.explanation: The description must have seven fields: sex, skin color, hair color, approximate age, height, weight and other features.

source.title: DCWP Educational Materials for Process Servers (PDF, updated 3/3/2025)
source.quote: a description of the person served which must consist of seven fields

questions.question: In the records, what does the service-type code "C" mean?
questions.explanation: C is conspicuous service; CO is corporate service.

source.title: DCWP Educational Materials for Process Servers (PDF, updated 3/3/2025)
source.quote: an S for substituted service, a C for conspicuous service delivery

questions.question: Which service-type code is used for corporate service?
questions.explanation: CO stands for corporate service.

source.title: DCWP Educational Materials for Process Servers (PDF, updated 3/3/2025)
source.quote: a CO for corporate service

questions.question: For affix-and-mail (CPLR 308(4)) service, what extra description must the record include?
options: The defendant's car and license plate, if seen
The weather and lighting at the time of service
The building's age and number of floors
The door and adjacent area, including hallway wall color and composition
questions.explanation: Records describe the door and adjacent area, including color and composition of hallway walls and floor.

source.title: DCWP Educational Materials for Process Servers (PDF, updated 3/3/2025)
source.quote: a description of the door and the area adjacent including the color and composition of hallway walls

questions.question: If RPAPL 735(1) service uses registered or certified mail, what must be recorded?
questions.explanation: The record includes the postal receipt number of the registered or certified mail.

source.title: DCWP Educational Materials for Process Servers (PDF, updated 3/3/2025)
source.quote: the postal receipt number of registered or certified mail

questions.question: How long must a third-party records contractor keep the original electronic record unaltered?
questions.explanation: The contractor must keep the original record unaltered for at least seven years.

source.title: DCWP Educational Materials for Process Servers (PDF, updated 3/3/2025)
source.quote: maintain the original electronic record submitted by the process server unaltered for a period of not less than seven years

questions.question: How often must a third-party records contractor back up submitted data?
questions.explanation: The contractor must maintain a daily backup of all submitted data.

source.title: DCWP Educational Materials for Process Servers (PDF, updated 3/3/2025)
source.quote: maintain a daily backup of all submitted data

questions.question: How long must a licensee keep a copy of each affidavit or affirmation of service?
options: One year, unless a traverse hearing is scheduled
Three years, in paper form only
At least seven years, electronically or on paper
Until the case is decided, then they may be discarded
questions.explanation: Keep a copy of each affidavit and affirmation of service for at least seven years.

source.title: DCWP Educational Materials for Process Servers (PDF, updated 3/3/2025)
source.quote: maintain a copy of each affidavit of service and affirmation of service for at least seven years

questions.question: Records are kept with a third party. Does that excuse a server from producing them to DCWP?
options: Only for records under a year old
No, they must still produce each requested record
Yes, DCWP must ask the contractor
questions.explanation: Servers must produce subpoenaed or requested records even where a third party maintains them.

source.title: DCWP Educational Materials for Process Servers (PDF, updated 3/3/2025)
source.quote: even where they maintain their records with a third party.

questions.question: Under GBL § 89-cc, what must the record include for service under CPLR 308(4)?
options: The color of the door to which the summons was affixed
The name of the building superintendent
questions.explanation: GBL § 89-cc requires a description of the color of the door the summons was affixed to.

source.title: DCWP Educational Materials for Process Servers (PDF, updated 3/3/2025)
source.quote: a description of the color of the door to which the summons is affixed

questions.question: If required records are lost or stolen, when must the licensee report it to DCWP?
options: Within ten calendar days, by affidavit
questions.explanation: Loss or theft of required records must be reported by affidavit within ten calendar days.

source.title: DCWP Educational Materials for Process Servers (PDF, updated 3/3/2025)
source.quote: within ten calendar days of such loss or theft.

questions.question: When must a process server carry the GPS-enabled device required by Admin Code § 20-410?
options: Only when serving papers in Housing Court cases
Only when serving corporations and other businesses
At all times during licensed activities, operating it when serving or attempting
Only when the assigning agency requires it
questions.explanation: The device must be carried at all times during licensed activities and operated at each service or attempt.

source.title: DCWP Educational Materials for Process Servers (PDF, updated 3/3/2025)
source.quote: carry at all times during the commission of his or her licensed activities and operate at the time process is served or attempted

questions.question: How long must GPS records of service be maintained?
questions.explanation: Device records are kept in an electronic database for seven years.

source.title: DCWP Educational Materials for Process Servers (PDF, updated 3/3/2025)
source.quote: for seven (7) years from the date such record is created.

questions.question: If no GPS signal is available at the moment of service, how is location determined?
options: By the defendant's address on the papers
questions.explanation: Without GPS, location, time and date come from triangulated cell tower signals.

source.title: DCWP Educational Materials for Process Servers (PDF, updated 3/3/2025)
source.quote: the location, time and date will be determined by triangulated cell tower signals.

questions.question: When must the GPS electronic record be made?
options: Immediately after the attempted or effected service
Before knocking on the door, to log the arrival
At the end of the day, for all attempts together
When the affidavit of service is signed
questions.explanation: The record is made immediately after the attempt; a record made before the attempt is non-compliant.

source.title: DCWP Educational Materials for Process Servers (PDF, updated 3/3/2025)
source.quote: The process server is not in compliance with this provision if its electronic record was made before the time of attempted or effected service.

questions.question: A GPS record is made more than how many minutes after service before non-compliance is presumed?
questions.explanation: There is a rebuttable presumption of non-compliance if the record is made more than five minutes after service.

source.title: DCWP Educational Materials for Process Servers (PDF, updated 3/3/2025)
source.quote: rebuttable presumption that the process server was not in compliance with this provision if its electronic record is made more than five minutes after

questions.question: In what format must the GPS record's latitude and longitude be given?
questions.explanation: Coordinates returned by the GPS device are recorded in decimal degree format.

source.title: DCWP Educational Materials for Process Servers (PDF, updated 3/3/2025)
source.quote: latitudinal and longitudinal coordinates returned by the GPS device in decimal degree format

questions.question: When must the GPS electronic record be transmitted to the GPS Contractor?
options: Weekly, when the server uploads the week's records
At license renewal, for the full license term
Only when DCWP asks for the records in an audit
Automatically, as soon as a GPS or cellular signal is available
questions.explanation: The record is automatically transmitted from the device as soon as a signal is available.

source.title: DCWP Educational Materials for Process Servers (PDF, updated 3/3/2025)
source.quote: must be automatically transmitted electronically from the mobile device to the GPS Contractor as soon as a GPS or cellular signal is available

questions.question: When is a GPS contractor NOT "independent" of a process serving agency?
options: When an agency officer or 10%+ owner has an interest
When it charges servers a monthly fee
When it serves more than one agency
When it is located outside New York State
questions.explanation: A third party is not independent if any agency officer or 10%+ shareholder has any direct or indirect interest in it.

source.title: DCWP Educational Materials for Process Servers (PDF, updated 3/3/2025)
source.quote: will not be considered independent if any officer or owner of ten percent or more of the shares of the licensed process serving agency

questions.question: A process server switches to a different GPS contractor. How soon must they file an amended certification?
questions.explanation: An amended certification is due within two days of contracting with a different GPS contractor.

source.title: DCWP Educational Materials for Process Servers (PDF, updated 3/3/2025)
source.quote: A licensed process server must submit to the Department an amended certification within two days of entering into a contract with a different GPS Contractor.

questions.question: On request, what map must the GPS contractor provide to the server or DCWP?
options: A hand-drawn sketch of each location, if asked
A hard-copy street map and an interactive e-map
Only a satellite photo of each address served
No map; only a spreadsheet of coordinates
questions.explanation: GPS contractors provide a hard-copy street map and an interactive electronic map showing where records were made.

source.title: DCWP Educational Materials for Process Servers (PDF, updated 3/3/2025)
source.quote: a street map in hard copy format and access to an interactive electronic street map

questions.question: May a process server who works for a licensed agency use the agency's GPS device and contractor?
options: No, every server needs their own contract
Yes, under the agency's GPS contract
questions.explanation: A server doing agency work may use the device and facilities the agency obtains under a GPS contract.

source.title: DCWP Process Server Individual Electronic Device Certification (PDF)
source.quote: The Process Serving Agency for whom I serve process will provide me with the device and services required by 6 RCNY section 2-233b.

questions.question: When may a licensee sign an affirmation of service or have an affidavit of service notarized?
options: Whenever the assigning agency asks for it
Before going out, so the form is ready to file
Any time within 20 days, even if details are missing
Only after all factual averments have been set forth
questions.explanation: Do not sign or notarize until all factual averments are set forth in the document.

source.title: DCWP Educational Materials for Process Servers (PDF, updated 3/3/2025)
source.quote: until all factual averments have been set forth

questions.question: What must appear on every affidavit and affirmation of service a licensee signs?
questions.explanation: Licensees must include their license number on all affidavits and affirmations of service.

source.title: DCWP Educational Materials for Process Servers (PDF, updated 3/3/2025)
source.quote: The licensee must include their license number on all affidavits of service and affirmations of service signed by them.

questions.question: When serving a business through a person said to be its "managing agent," what must the affidavit state?
options: That the server asked if they could accept service and they said yes
Nothing beyond the address where papers were left
Only the person's first name and approximate age
The business's tax ID and state filing number
questions.explanation: The affidavit must state the server inquired whether the person was authorized and received an affirmative response, plus name, job and supporting facts.

source.title: DCWP Educational Materials for Process Servers (PDF, updated 3/3/2025)
source.quote: that the process server inquired if that individual was authorized to accept service and received an affirmative response

questions.question: What can DCWP do if a licensee is found to have made a false statement in an affidavit of service?
options: Deny, refuse to renew, suspend or revoke the license
Only issue a written warning to the licensee
Nothing, since perjury is only a court matter
Only fine the agency that assigned the papers
questions.explanation: A false statement in an affidavit or affirmation of service is grounds for denial, non-renewal, suspension or revocation.

source.title: DCWP Educational Materials for Process Servers (PDF, updated 3/3/2025)
source.quote: A licensee must not make any false statement in an affidavit of service or affirmation of service.

questions.question: Under CPLR 2106, how may an affirmation under penalty of perjury be used in a New York action?
options: Only in federal court, not in state court
Only in criminal cases, not in civil actions
In lieu of and with the same force as an affidavit
Only if it is also notarized by a notary public
questions.explanation: A statement affirmed under penalty of perjury may be used in place of an affidavit with the same effect.

source.title: DCWP Educational Materials for Process Servers (PDF, updated 3/3/2025)
source.quote: may be used in an action in New York in lieu of and with the same force and effect as an affidavit.

questions.question: Under CPLR 306(b), proof of personal delivery must describe the person served. Which item is listed?
questions.explanation: The description covers gender, race, hair color, approximate age, approximate weight and height, and other features.

source.title: DCWP Educational Materials for Process Servers (PDF, updated 3/3/2025)
source.quote: the process server’s perception of the person’s: gender, race, hair color, approximate age, approximate weight and height, and other identifying features.

questions.question: Under CPLR 306(c), what must proof of affix-and-mail service also specify?
options: The names of neighbors who were asked about the person
The weather and lighting conditions at each attempt
Only the date of the final, successful attempt
The dates, addresses and times of the earlier attempts
questions.explanation: Proof of 308(4) service must specify the dates, addresses and times of attempted service under 308(1)-(3).

source.title: DCWP Educational Materials for Process Servers (PDF, updated 3/3/2025)
source.quote: proof of service shall also specify the dates, addresses and the times of attempted service pursuant to subdivisions one, two or three of such section.

questions.question: In what form is proof of service made by a private process server, under CPLR 306(d)?
options: A receipt from the defendant only
questions.explanation: A sheriff or public officer uses a certificate; any other person uses an affidavit.

source.title: DCWP Educational Materials for Process Servers (PDF, updated 3/3/2025)
source.quote: in the form of an affidavit if made by any other person

questions.question: Under DRL § 232, what must an affidavit of service in a divorce action state about the defendant?
options: What the server knew about the defendant's identity and how they knew it
The grounds for divorce stated in the complaint
The defendant's income and employer at the time of service
The names and ages of any children of the marriage
questions.explanation: It must state what knowledge the server had that the person was the named defendant and how it was acquired.

source.title: DCWP Educational Materials for Process Servers (PDF, updated 3/3/2025)
source.quote: what knowledge the affiant or officer who executed the certificate had that he was the defendant named and how he acquired such knowledge

questions.question: In a divorce action where the complaint is not served with the summons, what must appear on the summons?
options: The name of the judge assigned to the divorce case
Nothing extra beyond the usual summons information
The bar number of the plaintiff's attorney
A legible notice of the nature of the action, such as "Action for a divorce"
questions.explanation: The summons face must show the nature of the action (e.g., "Action for a divorce") and any ancillary relief.

source.title: DCWP Educational Materials for Process Servers (PDF, updated 3/3/2025)
source.quote: the summons shall have legibly written or printed upon the face thereof

questions.question: Within how many days must a licensee report a scheduled traverse hearing to DCWP?
questions.explanation: Report a scheduled hearing contesting service within 10 days of receiving oral or written notice.

source.title: DCWP: Process Server Individual License Application Checklist
source.quote: must report a scheduled traverse hearing (hearing contesting service) to DCWP within 10 days of receiving oral or written notice.

questions.question: Does an oral communication about a scheduled traverse hearing trigger the reporting duty?
options: Only a subpoena to appear counts
Yes, any notice, even oral, counts
Only a notice sent by DCWP counts
No, only written notice from the court
questions.explanation: Any type of notice, including oral, triggers the 10-day report.

source.title: DCWP Educational Materials for Process Servers (PDF, updated 3/3/2025)
source.quote: receives any type of notice, including an oral communication, that a court has scheduled a hearing

questions.question: Which of these must the traverse hearing report include?
options: The server's fee and the agency that paid it
The defendant's phone number and date of birth
The court and the judge before whom the hearing is scheduled
The assigning agency's bank and billing details
questions.explanation: The report includes title and index number, court and judge, hearing date(s), and every licensee involved.

source.title: DCWP Educational Materials for Process Servers (PDF, updated 3/3/2025)
source.quote: the court and the judge before whom the hearing is scheduled

questions.question: If the party has not reported a traverse hearing's result, when must the licensee first search the court clerk's file?
options: Ten days after the scheduled hearing
One year after the scheduled hearing
Sixty days after the scheduled hearing
The day after the scheduled hearing
questions.explanation: At sixty days without a written report from the party, search the clerk's file; if needed, search again at ninety days.

source.title: DCWP Educational Materials for Process Servers (PDF, updated 3/3/2025)
source.quote: Sixty days after the date of the scheduled hearing, if the party or its attorney has not provided to the licensee a written report

questions.question: If a licensee cannot learn a traverse hearing's result, by when must they report that to DCWP?
options: They need not report if the result is unknown
No later than 30 days after the hearing
No later than one year after the hearing
No later than 100 days after the scheduled hearing
questions.explanation: Report the result within ten days of learning it, or report unsuccessful attempts no later than 100 days after the hearing date.

source.title: DCWP Educational Materials for Process Servers (PDF, updated 3/3/2025)
source.quote: not later than one-hundred days after the scheduled date of such hearing.

questions.question: What must a licensed process server bring to a NYC Civil Court traverse hearing at which they testify?
options: All related records, and their license
Nothing; the court has the records
questions.explanation: Rule 208.29 requires all relevant records, and a licensed server must also bring the license.

source.title: DCWP Educational Materials for Process Servers (PDF, updated 3/3/2025)
source.quote: Where the process server is licensed, he or she also shall bring the license to the court.

questions.question: May a licensee wear a badge or shield while serving process?
options: No, badges, insignia and shields are prohibited
questions.explanation: No licensee serving process may wear or display any badge, insignia, shield, medal or facsimile.

source.title: DCWP Educational Materials for Process Servers (PDF, updated 3/3/2025)
source.quote: No licensee while serving process shall wear or display any badge, insignia, shield, medal, decoration or facsimile thereof.

questions.question: What must the envelope for process mailed under CPLR 308(4) or RPAPL 735(1) include?
options: The proper ZIP code of the person served
questions.explanation: Mailed copies must include the proper ZIP code in the address.

source.title: DCWP Educational Materials for Process Servers (PDF, updated 3/3/2025)
source.quote: must include on the envelope as part of the address the proper ZIP code of the person served.

questions.question: What is the effect of serving civil process on a Sunday (absent a statutory exception)?
options: It is valid with court approval later
questions.explanation: GBL § 11 makes Sunday service void for every purpose, except in criminal proceedings or where a statute authorizes it.

source.title: DCWP Educational Materials for Process Servers (PDF, updated 3/3/2025)
source.quote: Service or execution of any process upon said day except as herein permitted is absolutely void for any and every purpose whatsoever.

questions.question: Sunday service of process is allowed in which situation?
options: Housing Court cases only, for urgent evictions
Criminal proceedings, or where a statute specially authorizes it
Any case, if the defendant agrees to accept it
Small claims cases, if the court clerk approves it
questions.explanation: GBL § 11 excepts criminal proceedings and service specially authorized by statute.

source.title: DCWP Educational Materials for Process Servers (PDF, updated 3/3/2025)
source.quote: except in criminal proceedings or where service or execution is specially authorized by statute.

questions.question: Maliciously serving civil process on Saturday on someone who keeps Saturday as holy time is:
questions.explanation: GBL § 13 makes this a misdemeanor.

source.title: DCWP Educational Materials for Process Servers (PDF, updated 3/3/2025)
source.quote: maliciously procures any civil action to which such person is a party to be adjourned to that day for trial, is guilty of a misdemeanor

questions.question: Under GBL § 89-bb, a person is a process server if they derive income from serving papers or did what?
options: Served at least once in the past calendar year
Effected service in five or more actions in the prior twelve months
Holds a notary public commission in the state
Works for a law firm as a clerk or paralegal
questions.explanation: The state definition includes anyone who served process in five or more actions in the preceding twelve months.

source.title: DCWP Educational Materials for Process Servers (PDF, updated 3/3/2025)
source.quote: has effected service of process in five or more actions or proceedings in the twelve month period immediately preceding the service in question.

questions.question: Under GBL § 89-ee, when is a process serving agency legally responsible for a server's acts?
options: If it could reasonably have known the server was acting improperly
Only if the server is the agency's W-2 employee
Never; each server alone is responsible
Only after DCWP has fined the server
questions.explanation: An agency is responsible if it could reasonably have known the server was acting improperly.

source.title: DCWP Educational Materials for Process Servers (PDF, updated 3/3/2025)
source.quote: if it could reasonably have known that the process server was acting improperly.

questions.question: Under CPLR 308(2), within what period of each other must delivery to a person of suitable age and the mailing occur?
questions.explanation: Delivery and mailing must be effected within twenty days of each other.

source.title: DCWP Educational Materials for Process Servers (PDF, updated 3/3/2025)
source.quote: such delivery and mailing to be effected within twenty days of each other

questions.question: Under CPLR 308(2), when is service complete?
options: Ten days after proof is filed
questions.explanation: Service is complete ten days after filing proof of service.

source.title: DCWP Educational Materials for Process Servers (PDF, updated 3/3/2025)
source.quote: service shall be complete ten days after such filing

questions.question: How must the envelope be marked when mailing to a defendant's actual place of business under CPLR 308(2)?
questions.explanation: The envelope bears the legend "personal and confidential" and must not show it is from an attorney or about a lawsuit.

source.title: DCWP Educational Materials for Process Servers (PDF, updated 3/3/2025)
source.quote: in an envelope bearing the legend "personal and confidential"

questions.question: What must the business-address envelope NOT indicate under CPLR 308(2) and 308(4)?
options: That it is from an attorney or concerns an action against the person
The person's name, as it appears on the papers
The ZIP code of the person being served
The street address, including the apartment number
questions.explanation: Nothing on the outside may indicate it is from an attorney or concerns an action against the person.

source.title: DCWP Educational Materials for Process Servers (PDF, updated 3/3/2025)
source.quote: not indicating on the outside thereof, by return address or otherwise, that the communication is from an attorney

questions.question: Within how long must proof of CPLR 308(2) service be filed with the court clerk?
options: Within twenty days of the delivery or mailing, whichever is later
Within three days of delivery, as with eviction papers
Before the mailing is sent, along with the affidavit
Within 120 days of filing the summons and complaint
questions.explanation: Proof must be filed within twenty days of the later of delivery or mailing.

source.title: DCWP Educational Materials for Process Servers (PDF, updated 3/3/2025)
source.quote: proof of such service shall be filed with the clerk of the court designated in the summons within twenty days

questions.question: When may a server use affix-and-mail ("nail and mail") service under CPLR 308(4)?
options: Only if 308(1) and (2) fail despite due diligence
Whenever the defendant is not home on one visit
Whenever the server chooses, as a first option
Only on weekends, when no one answers the door
questions.explanation: Affixing to the door is allowed only where personal and substituted service cannot be made with due diligence.

source.title: DCWP Educational Materials for Process Servers (PDF, updated 3/3/2025)
source.quote: where service under paragraphs one and two cannot be made with due diligence, by affixing the summons to the door

questions.question: When may service be made in a manner the court directs under CPLR 308(5)?
options: Only after the 120-day service period has run
Only when serving corporations and LLCs
When service under 308(1), (2) and (4) is impracticable
Whenever the plaintiff prefers a faster method
questions.explanation: A court may direct another method on motion without notice when the standard methods are impracticable.

source.title: DCWP Educational Materials for Process Servers (PDF, updated 3/3/2025)
source.quote: in such manner as the court, upon motion without notice, directs, if service is impracticable under paragraphs one, two and four of this section.

questions.question: Under CPLR 308(6), what counts as a defendant's "actual place of business"?
options: Any place it held out as its business by regular ads or solicitation
The defendant's home, if the defendant works from home
Only the business address on file with the Department of State
Only an office the defendant leases or owns in its own name
questions.explanation: It includes any location the defendant held out as its place of business through regular solicitation or advertisement.

source.title: DCWP Educational Materials for Process Servers (PDF, updated 3/3/2025)
source.quote: shall include any location that the defendant, through regular solicitation or advertisement, has held out as its place of business.

questions.question: Under CPLR 306-b, within how long after commencing an action must the summons and complaint generally be served?
questions.explanation: Service is due within 120 days after commencement (with a shorter rule for short limitation periods).

source.title: DCWP Educational Materials for Process Servers (PDF, updated 3/3/2025)
source.quote: shall be made within one hundred twenty days after the commencement of the action or proceeding

questions.question: If the statute of limitations is four months or less, when must service be made under CPLR 306-b?
options: Before the summons is filed with the court
Within 3 days after the limitations period expires
No later than 15 days after the limitations period expires
Within 120 days of filing, as in any other action
questions.explanation: For short limitation periods, service must be made within 15 days after the statute of limitations expires.

source.title: DCWP Educational Materials for Process Servers (PDF, updated 3/3/2025)
source.quote: service shall be made not later than fifteen days after the date on which the applicable statute of limitations expires.

questions.question: How is personal service made on the State of New York?
options: Deliver it to the Secretary of State in Albany only
Deliver it to any state employee at a state office
Mail it by certified mail to the Governor's office
Deliver to an assistant attorney-general at an AG office, or to the attorney-general
questions.explanation: Personal service upon the state is by delivery to an assistant attorney-general at an AG office, or to the attorney-general, within the state.

source.title: DCWP Educational Materials for Process Servers (PDF, updated 3/3/2025)
source.quote: delivering the summons to an assistant attorney-general at an office of the attorney-general or to the attorney-general within the state

questions.question: Certified-mail service on a state agency under CPLR 307 is effective only if the envelope front bears what?
questions.explanation: The front must bear the legend URGENT LEGAL MAIL in capitals.

source.title: DCWP Educational Materials for Process Servers (PDF, updated 3/3/2025)
source.quote: Service by certified mail shall not be effective unless the front of the envelope bears the legend "URGENT LEGAL MAIL" in capital letters.

questions.question: Serving a summons on a 15-year-old, who must be personally served under CPLR 309(a)?
options: The child's school principal, as custodian
Only a parent, since the child is a minor
Only the child, since the child is over 14
A parent, guardian or custodian, and also the child
questions.explanation: Serve a parent, guardian or person with legal custody; an infant aged 14 or over must also be personally served.

source.title: DCWP Educational Materials for Process Servers (PDF, updated 3/3/2025)
source.quote: If the infant is of the age of fourteen years or over, the summons shall also be personally served upon him within the state.

questions.question: How may personal service be made on persons doing business as a partnership under CPLR 310(a)?
options: Only through the Secretary of State
By personally serving any one of the partners
questions.explanation: Personal service may be made by personally serving any one of the partners.

source.title: DCWP Educational Materials for Process Servers (PDF, updated 3/3/2025)
source.quote: Personal service upon persons conducting a business as a partnership may be made by personally serving the summons upon any one of them.

questions.question: Under CPLR 311(a)(1), which person can accept service for a corporation?
options: Any employee working at the front desk
An officer, director, managing or general agent, or cashier
questions.explanation: Delivery may be to an officer, director, managing or general agent, cashier or assistant cashier, or an authorized agent.

source.title: DCWP Educational Materials for Process Servers (PDF, updated 3/3/2025)
source.quote: to an officer, director, managing or general agent, or cashier or assistant cashier or to any other agent authorized by appointment or by law

questions.question: How is personal service made on the City of New York?
options: Deliver it to the head of any City agency involved
Deliver it to the Corporation Counsel or a filed designee
Mail it by certified mail to City Hall in Manhattan
Deliver it to the Mayor or a deputy mayor at City Hall
questions.explanation: Service on the City is made on the Corporation Counsel or a person designated in a writing filed with the New York County clerk.

source.title: DCWP Educational Materials for Process Servers (PDF, updated 3/3/2025)
source.quote: upon the city of New York, to the corporation counsel

questions.question: Under CPLR 311, whom may a server deliver a summons to when serving a town?
questions.explanation: Service on a town is made on the supervisor or the clerk.

source.title: DCWP Educational Materials for Process Servers (PDF, updated 3/3/2025)
source.quote: upon a town, to the supervisor or the clerk

questions.question: For a member-managed LLC, to whom may process be delivered under CPLR 311-a?
options: Any member of the LLC in New York
questions.explanation: If management is vested in members, delivery to any member in the state works.

source.title: DCWP Educational Materials for Process Servers (PDF, updated 3/3/2025)
source.quote: any member of the limited liability company in this state, if the management of the limited liability company is vested in its members

questions.question: How may personal service be made on a court of three or more judges?
options: Mail it to the chief judge
Deliver the summons to any one of the judges
Deliver to the court clerk only
questions.explanation: Delivery to any one of the judges suffices.

source.title: DCWP Educational Materials for Process Servers (PDF, updated 3/3/2025)
source.quote: Personal service upon a court consisting of three or more judges may be made by delivering the summons to any one of them.

questions.question: Under Civil Court Act § 403, where must service of a NYC Civil Court summons generally be made?
options: Only within the City of New York, unless otherwise authorized
Anywhere in the United States, by any method
Only in the county where the case was filed
Anywhere in New York State, as in Supreme Court
questions.explanation: Civil Court summonses are served only within NYC unless service beyond is authorized.

source.title: DCWP Educational Materials for Process Servers (PDF, updated 3/3/2025)
source.quote: but it shall be made only within the city of New York unless service beyond the city be authorized by this act

questions.question: What must appear on a Civil Court summons as served, under CCA § 400?
questions.explanation: The actual index number must be on the summons, notice of petition or order to show cause as served.

source.title: DCWP Educational Materials for Process Servers (PDF, updated 3/3/2025)
source.quote: The actual index number shall be on the summons, notice of petition or order to show cause as served.

questions.question: What is "VTL service" under the DCWP rules?
options: Serving a non-resident via the Secretary of State (VTL § 253)
Serving papers on drivers by text message
Serving traffic tickets on behalf of the NYPD
Serving papers on drivers at a DMV office
questions.explanation: VTL service includes service on a non-resident through the Secretary of State under VTL § 253.

source.title: DCWP Educational Materials for Process Servers (PDF, updated 3/3/2025)
source.quote: a non-resident by service on the Secretary of State as permitted by and in accordance with the provisions of Vehicle and Traffic Law § 253

questions.question: What is "substituted service" under the DCWP rules?
options: Service carried out by court officers instead of a server
Delivery to anyone found at the address, of any age
Service by email to the person's last known address
Delivery to a person of suitable age and discretion at the home or business
questions.explanation: Substituted service is delivery within the state to a person of suitable age and discretion at the actual place of business, dwelling or usual abode.

source.title: DCWP Educational Materials for Process Servers (PDF, updated 3/3/2025)
source.quote: delivering process within the state to an individual of suitable age and discretion at the actual place of business, dwelling place

questions.question: After substituted or conspicuous service of a notice of petition under RPAPL 735, when must it be mailed?
questions.explanation: Mailing must follow within one day after the delivery, affixing or placement.

source.title: DCWP Educational Materials for Process Servers (PDF, updated 3/3/2025)
source.quote: within one day after such delivering to such suitable person or such affixing or placement, by mailing to the respondent

questions.question: How must those RPAPL 735 papers be mailed?
options: By registered or certified mail only
By regular first class mail only
By certified (or registered) and first class mail
By email plus regular first class mail
questions.explanation: Both registered or certified mail and regular first class mail are required.

source.title: DCWP Educational Materials for Process Servers (PDF, updated 3/3/2025)
source.quote: both by registered or certified mail and by regular first class mail

questions.question: Within how long must the notice of petition and proof of service be filed with the court under RPAPL 735?
questions.explanation: They must be filed within three days after personal delivery or after mailing.

source.title: DCWP Educational Materials for Process Servers (PDF, updated 3/3/2025)
source.quote: together with proof of service thereof shall be filed with the court or clerk thereof within three days after

questions.question: Under RPAPL 735, when is personal delivery to the respondent complete?
questions.explanation: Personal delivery service is complete immediately upon delivery.

source.title: DCWP Educational Materials for Process Servers (PDF, updated 3/3/2025)
source.quote: such service shall be complete immediately upon such personal delivery

questions.question: Under RPAPL 735, when is substituted or conspicuous service complete?
options: Upon the filing of proof of service
questions.explanation: With the alternative methods, service is complete when proof of service is filed.

source.title: DCWP Educational Materials for Process Servers (PDF, updated 3/3/2025)
source.quote: such service shall be complete upon the filing of proof of service.

questions.question: Under RPAPL 735, besides affixing to a conspicuous part of the property, what else may a server do if admittance cannot be obtained?
options: Hand it to the super at another building
Place a copy under the entrance door
questions.explanation: The papers may be affixed to a conspicuous part of the property or placed under the entrance door.

source.title: DCWP Educational Materials for Process Servers (PDF, updated 3/3/2025)
source.quote: placing a copy under the entrance door of such premises

questions.question: Under BCL § 306, where is in-person service on the Secretary of State made?
options: At the Department of State office in Albany
questions.explanation: Duplicate copies with the statutory fee are delivered at the Department of State office in Albany.

source.title: DCWP Educational Materials for Process Servers (PDF, updated 3/3/2025)
source.quote: at the office of the department of state in the city of Albany, duplicate copies of such process together with the statutory fee

questions.question: When is in-person service on a corporation through the Secretary of State complete?
options: When the corporation receives the mail
When the Secretary of State is served
questions.explanation: Service is complete when the Secretary of State is served.

source.title: DCWP Educational Materials for Process Servers (PDF, updated 3/3/2025)
source.quote: Service of process on such corporation shall be complete when the secretary of state is so served.

questions.question: When is electronic service through the Department of State complete under BCL § 306?
options: When the corporation opens the notice
When the Department of State's email is sent out
Ten days after the process is submitted
When the Secretary of State has reviewed and accepted it
questions.explanation: Electronic service is complete when the Secretary of State has reviewed and accepted service.

source.title: DCWP Educational Materials for Process Servers (PDF, updated 3/3/2025)
source.quote: Service of process on such corporation shall be complete when the secretary of state has reviewed and accepted service of such process.

questions.question: How often must a process serving agency review the records of each server it assigns work to?
questions.explanation: Agencies review each server's records for completeness and accuracy at least monthly.

source.title: DCWP Educational Materials for Process Servers (PDF, updated 3/3/2025)
source.quote: at least once each month, review for completeness and accuracy the records of each individual process server

questions.question: How soon must an agency report a non-compliant process server to DCWP?
options: At the agency's next license renewal
Within 24 hours of learning of it
Within 30 days of learning of it
Within ten days of learning of it
questions.explanation: Agencies report non-compliant servers' names and license numbers within ten days.

source.title: DCWP Educational Materials for Process Servers (PDF, updated 3/3/2025)
source.quote: within ten (10) days of learning of such non-compliance

questions.question: How long must an agency keep each employee's signed statement of rights and obligations?
questions.explanation: The signed statement is kept on file at the principal place of business for three years.

source.title: DCWP Educational Materials for Process Servers (PDF, updated 3/3/2025)
source.quote: Keep on file in its principal place of business for a period of three (3) years a statement for each employee

questions.question: At minimum, what share of certifying process servers must DCWP audit each year?
questions.explanation: DCWP audits at least 20% of servers who certified serving Civil Court Act § 110 process.

source.title: DCWP Educational Materials for Process Servers (PDF, updated 3/3/2025)
source.quote: for at least 20 percent of the licensed process servers who have certified

questions.question: In an audit, what is the longest period of records a DCWP subpoena may cover?
questions.explanation: The audit subpoena period is no longer than two months.

source.title: DCWP Educational Materials for Process Servers (PDF, updated 3/3/2025)
source.quote: for the period identified by the Department in such subpoena for the following records no longer than two months

questions.question: How soon must a process server comply with a DCWP audit subpoena?
questions.explanation: Each document demand must be met within 20 days of the date the subpoena was issued.

source.title: DCWP Educational Materials for Process Servers (PDF, updated 3/3/2025)
source.quote: within 20 days of the date on which the subpoena was issued

questions.question: The housing court certification concerns process subject to which statute?
options: Section 110 of the Civil Court Act
General Business Law § 11, on Sunday service
CPLR 306-b, on the time limit for service
questions.explanation: Servers certify whether they served process subject to Civil Court Act § 110 (housing court).

source.title: DCWP Educational Materials for Process Servers (PDF, updated 3/3/2025)
source.quote: that is subject to the provisions of section 110 of the civil court act
